newsitem.title: INDIA: Events during India's 50 years of independence.
newsitem.headline: Events during India's 50 years of independence.

text.p: Following is a chronology of major Indian events during the past 50 years after the country won freedom from British colonial rule on August 15, 1947.
August 15, 1947: India wins independence from Britain after being divided into two separate nations, India and Pakistan. Jawaharlal Nehru is appointed the first prime minister.
October 27, 1947: War breaks out between Indian and Pakistani troops in the disputed Himalayan region of Kashmir.
January 30, 1948: Mahatma Gandhi, leader of the independence movement and champion of non-violent protest, is assassinated.
January 1, 1949: Ceasefire, ordered by the United Nations Security Council, takes effect in Himalayan territory of Kashmir.
January 26, 1950: India becomes a republic as its constitution comes into effect.
1951: India launches its first five-year plan.
October 25, 1951-February 21, 1952: India holds first general elections.
1962: Indian army liberates enclave of Goa from Portuguese colonial rule. India and China fight a brief war over a border dispute.
1963: India launches its first rocket into space.
May 27, 1964: Jawaharlal Nehru dies after a five-month illness.
September 6-22, 1965: Full-scale India-Pakistan war over Kashmir, which ends after a U.N. call for ceasefire.
January 3, 1966: Indian Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri and Pakistani President Ayub Khan sign a Soviet-mediated peace pact in Tashkent, then part of the Soviet Uzbek republic.
January, 1966: Supported by provincial Congress chief ministers, Nehru's daughter Indira Gandhi becomes prime minister. India launches a green revolution aimed at boosting its agriculture produce.
December 3-17, 1971: India and Pakistan fight second major war over East Pakistan (later Bangladesh) which ends after 90,000 Pakistani troops surrender.
July 2, 1972: Indian Prime Minister Indira Gandhi and Pakistani Prime Minister Zulfikar Ali Bhutto sign a peace accord in Simla, India.
May 18, 1974: India conducts underground nuclear test which it says is for its atomic energy programme, not weapons.
April 19, 1975: First Indian satellite Aryabhatta goes into earth's orbit.
June 26, 1975: A state of emergency is declared during which press is censored, 100,000 are jailed.
1977: First non-Congress government sweeps to power following Indira Gandhi's defeat at the general elections.

November 1977: More than 10,000 people die when a cyclone hits India's southeast coast. The storm disrupts life for 5.4 million people in 830 villages, and damages 1.4 million hectares (3.5 million acres) of cropland.
January 1980: Indira Gandhi wins back power, sworn in as prime minister.

June 1984: Indira Gandhi dispatches troops into Amritsar's Golden Temple, Sikhdom's holiest shrine. More than 1,000 people are killed in the operation to oust separatist militants using the temple as a headquarters.

October 31, 1984: Indira Gandhi is assassinated by Sikh bodyguards in retaliation for dispatching troops to the Golden temple. Her son Rajiv Gandhi takes over as prime minister with India in turmoil as Hindus kill some 2,700 Sikhs in revenge riots.

December 1984 - Deadly gas leaks from a pesticide plant owned by U.S.-based Union Carbide Corp in central city of Bhopal, killing some 6,500 people and injuring 20,000 in world's worst industrial disaster.

June 23, 1985: Air-India plane explodes and crashes into sea off the coast of Ireland, killing 329 people. Sikh extremists claim responsibility. India becomes a member of the South Asian Association for Regional Co-operation (SAARC).
1986: The Gorkha National Liberation Front launches a movement for a separate homeland in India's northeast.
December 31, 1988: India and Pakistan sign agreement not to attack each other's nuclear facilities.
January 1990: An uprising against Indian rule in the Kashmir Valley breaks out, inflaming tensions with Pakistan. New Delhi dissolves the state assembly and imposes direct rule.
May 1990: A cyclone ravages southern state of Andhra Pradesh, killing nearly 1,000 people.
May 21, 1991 - Former prime minister Rajiv Gandhi, who sent troops to Sri Lanka in 1987, is assassinated by Tamil suicide bomber in southern India during election campaign.
Congress party wins in general elections and India launches sweeping economic reforms by opening up trade and industry and dismantles decades of socialist control.
December 6, 1992: Hindu zealots tear down a 16th century mosque in the northern town of Ayodhya, sparking nationwide riots in which some 3,000 people, mostly Moslems, die.
March 12, 1993: A series of bomb blasts, thought to be planted by Moslem underworld figures, rock the country's commercial capital of Bombay, killing some 260 people.
January 26, 1994: India rolls out short-range Prithvi missile at Republic Day Parade in New Delhi.
December 23, 1995: Nearly 425 people die when a blaze rips through a school prize-giving ceremony in the northern town of Dabwali in Haryana state, near the Indian capital.
June 28, 1996: Communists join the government for first time since independence, four weeks after 13-party coalition takes power following general elections in which Congress is ousted.
November 12, 1996: A Saudi Arabian Boeing 747 jumbo jet and a Kazakhstan Ilyushin cargo plane collide near New Delhi, killing 349 people in the world's deadliest mid-air collision.
